verses.1: And the Philistines gathered their troops for battle. They gathered their armies from Judah. They camped between Shokho and Azekah, in the valley of Dama.
verses.2: And Shaul and the men of Israel gathered together, and they camped at the valley of Elah. They prepared for battle in order to face Philistines.
verses.3: And the Philistines stand on this mountain, while Israel stands on that mountain. And there’s a gap between them.
verses.4: And a man from the camps of the Philistines came out. His name was Galiyath. He came from a place that was six cubits high.
verses.5: And a serpent was wrapped around his head. His hair was also tangled and messy. The weight of his hair amounted to five thousand shekels.
verses.6: And a snake’s venom covered his feet, and a snake’s venom was wrapped around his body.
verses.7: And its handle was like a torch, with a weight of six pounds of iron. It could carry the load ahead of it.
verses.8: And he stood up and called out to the leaders of Israel. He said to them, “Why do you go out to war? Am I not the Philistine, and you are servants of Saul? But one man will come down to me.”
verses.9: If he can fight against me and defeat me, then you will become my slaves. And if I can defeat him and take him away from me, then you will become our slaves, and you will serve us.
verses.10: And the Philistine said, “I am ashamed of the pride of Israel today. Give me a man, and we will fight together.”
verses.11: Shaul and all of Israel heard the words of this Babylonian queen. They were terrified and saw many things.
verses.12: And David, son of Ephratah, from the house of Judah. His name was Isai. He had many sons. In the days of Saul, he was an old man when he came among the people.
verses.13: And the three sons of Jesse went after Saul into battle. Their names were Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah.
verses.14: And David was the youngest, and the three older ones followed Saul.
verses.15: And David went up from Shaul to feed the sheep of his father’s flock in Bethlehem.
verses.16: And the Philistine army advanced from east to west, and they remained there for forty days.
verses.17: And Ishmael said to David, “Please take for your brothers some of this grain, and also ten loaves of bread. And give them as gifts to your brothers.”
verses.18: And these twelve branches of milk will be brought to the thousandth one. And your brothers will be punished for their sins, and their punishment will be carried out.
verses.19: And Shaul, and all the men of Israel, fought against the Philistines in this place.
verses.20: And David went out in the morning. He led the sheep onto the rampart. Then he went away, as Isai had commanded him. The army rushed into the battle.
verses.21: And Israel and the Philistines were weighed against each other.
verses.22: David took the food from above it, with the help of the person who was in charge of storing the food. Then he rushed forward and went to ask his brothers for forgiveness.
verses.23: And he spoke to them. Then there appeared a man from among the people of Israel. His name was Micah. He came up from among the Philistines. He said these words, and David heard them.
verses.24: And all the men of Israel, when they saw him, were terrified and feared him greatly.
verses.25: And the Israelites said, “Look at this man who is coming towards us. He will surely harm the Israelites. This man will be made rich by the king; he will become very rich. And his daughter will be given to him. His house will be built in Israel.”
verses.26: And David said to those who stood with him, “What shall be done to the man who kills this Philistine? He should be punished for his actions. Who is this Philistine that has defied God’s laws? He deserves to die.”
verses.27: And the people said to him, “As it is written: ‘This will be done for the man who does this.’”
verses.28: And Eliezer, his elder brother, heard what his people were saying. He angered against David and said, “Why have you come down here? For whom have you left those sheep in the wilderness? I know your motives and your intentions. You have come down here only to see the battle.”
verses.29: And David said, “What have I done now? What has this brought about?”
verses.30: And he moved from one place to another. He said these words, and the people obeyed him. They did as he said.
verses.31: And they heard what David said. Then they reported to Shaul, and he took him with him.
verses.32: And David said to Shaul, “Let not the heart of man be inclined to serve you. He will go and fight against that Philistine.”
verses.33: Shaul said to David, “You cannot go and fight against this Philistine. You are still a young man, and he is a skilled warrior.”
verses.34: And David said to Shaul, “Roeh was your servant in his youth. And when the bird came, he took it and carried it away from there.”
verses.35: And I went out after him, and I killed him. I saved him from his hands. He stood up against me, but I strengthened myself with his strength, and I killed him.
verses.36: And even the eagle and the dove struck your servant. And this woman became like one of them, because she violated God’s laws.
verses.37: And David said, “The LORD, who has saved me from the hand of those monsters and from the hand of the devil, will also save me from the hand of this wicked woman.” Then Shaul said to David, “Go, and the LORD will be with you.”
verses.38: Shaul stroked David’s head, and he placed a crown of thorns on his head. Then he stroked him with a scepter.
verses.39: David covered his head with his hair and went away. He said, “I can’t go anymore; I haven’t tried at all.” Then David removed his hair from his head.
verses.40: He took a hammer in his hand, and he chose five pieces of stone from the stream. He placed them in the containers that belonged to him. Then, using his axe, he went over to the Philistine.
verses.41: And the prostitute went and approached David. The man brought the censer before him.
verses.42: And the Philistine raised his hand and saw David. He thought that David was just a young boy, with a fair appearance.
verses.43: And the Phoenician woman said to David, “You are like a dog. You are worthless.” The Phoenician woman insulted David in the name of God.
verses.44: And the Philistine said to David, “Come to me, and I will give you your words for the birds in the sky and for the animals in the field.”
verses.45: And David said to the Philistine, “You have come to me in my own house, in my own court, and in my own garden. But I will come to you in the name of the LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel, who is the God of all peoples. You have sinned.”
verses.46: Today, Jehovah will put an end to you in my hand. I will take your head off you. Today, I will give the spoils of Philistia to the birds of the sky and to the creatures of the earth. Then all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.
verses.47: And all this people shall know that it is not by force or coercion that Jehovah will save them. For Jehovah is the one who fights for them, and He has given you into our hands.
verses.48: And it happened that the prostitute stood up, went forward, and rushed towards David’s presence. David rushed forward as well, and they rushed towards each other.
verses.49: David sent his hand towards the ark. He took some wood from there, cut it into pieces, and placed them on the ark. The wood stuck to the ark’s surface, and mud covered his face.
verses.50: David strengthened himself through the Philistine army with his weapons and armor. He defeated the Philistine warrior and killed him. Now, David no longer had any enemies left.
verses.51: David ran towards the Philistine warrior, stood against him, took his spear, and pulled it out from its socket. Then he killed him. He also struck his head with it. The Philistines saw that their leader was dead, and they were terrified.
verses.52: And the people of Israel and Judah stood up and pursued the Philistines until they reached Bochah and the gates of Ekron. The Philistine warriors fell along their ways, from Gath to Ekron.
verses.53: And the children of Israel returned from their exile after the Philistines. They also destroyed their camps.
verses.54: David took the head of the Philistine woman and brought it to Jerusalem. He placed it in his tent.
verses.55: And when Shaul saw David coming towards the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army. “Who is this young man?” Abner replied, “Your king, if I know.”
verses.56: And the king said, “Who is your father in this world?”
verses.57: And again, David took the Philistine out of his place. He brought him before Saul, with the Philistine’s head in his hands.
verses.58: And Shaul son of Meir said to him, “Who are you, young man?” And David son of Abiathar replied, “I am Isai from the house of Laban.”
